Applicability is the public ReadOnlySafe RawNode promise: quorum communication supports a request-specific safe barrier. ReadIndex has no stated local-membership precondition, ApplyConfChange requires applying committed removals, and StepDownOnRemoval is an optional role-demotion setting rather than a waiver of safe-read output semantics. Continuing to invoke the removed RawNode is an explicit scope condition; no external service routing contract is assumed. The driver creates a common compacted prefix through public MemoryStorage, actually campaigns node 1 and commits ConfChangeRemoveNode(1), applies that entry through actual MsgStorageApply callbacks on both nodes, and verifies their sole incoming voter is node 2. It then actually campaigns node 2 and observes application of its new write. This is one legal history per option, with no internal role/config/log assignment after public initialization. Async append writes and application finish before their Responses are queued, and FIFO processing preserves caller duties. Ticks are omitted only over this finite schedule; neither side needs timeout progress because Campaign is invoked explicitly. The read call follows the write application observation. before_read admits exactly one operation per step_down boolean, and after_read follows the actual API return plus complete drain of generated Ready/messages; this is completion of the library observation interval, not an assertion of successful client read completion. The boolean identity separates independent variants, not compared output values. own_voter is read from the installed config, fresh_support counts actual newly delivered context-matching messages from the sole voter, and released counts matching Ready.ReadStates. Neither support nor release is precomputed. The implication evaluates release only when independent eligibility/support is false, and permits no output. For step_down=false, execution reports StateLeader at term 2 after remaining voter is term 3, own_voter=false, fresh_support=0, eligible_support=false, released=true, read_count=1 and read_index=3. For true it reports StateFollower, no eligible support and released=false. Both subtests finish normally. Source switchToConfig retains leader role when false; IsSingleton tests cardinality only; the read branch immediately emits local commit. The paired option changes role and blocks this observed path. Thus the measured failure corresponds to the accepted local authority-support requirement. It does not rely on the stronger and unchecked oracle that every returned index must equal or exceed the later write index, nor infer global linearizability from those numbers.

formation.explanation: A serialized RawNode.Propose (or node.run proposal event) enters raft.Step. A follower forwards to a known leader or drops; a candidate drops. A leader rejects transfer/removal/quota cases, assigns term/index, appends locally and broadcasts predecessor-qualified MsgApp. Followers check predecessor and committed-prefix conflicts, append only conflicting suffixes, bound advertised commit, and queue replies. Both follower replies and leader self-acks pass through msgsAfterAppend; legal publication relies on caller persistence, directly via Ready/Advance or ordered async append Responses. The leader term-filters replies and raises sender Match. Tracker considers only active voters, majority order statistics and both halves of joint configuration. raftLog.maybeCommit additionally requires the candidate entry to match the current term. Commit propagates via append or Match-capped heartbeat. Ready exports committed entries; async apply waits for local stability. Application and public client completion remain separate caller actions; proposal acceptance does not promise commitment.

context.explanation: Ticks or Campaign trigger hup only when promotable and without unapplied committed configuration changes. PreVote can gather prospective support without increasing term; real candidacy resets state, increments term and records self vote. Self and remote vote replies are queued behind persistence. Vote grants require vote/leader eligibility and last-log freshness. Matching response type and active voter quorum determine victory; the new leader resets progress and appends its current-term empty entry. Higher-term messages normally force follower transition, with lease/pre-vote exceptions; obsolete responses are rejected. CheckQuorum can cause same-term stepdown. Transfer pauses proposals, catches the target up and sends TimeoutNow; timeout or ineligibility aborts transfer. Restart restores HardState/log/configuration and starts as follower. Configuration entries activate through ApplyConfChange, changing voters and optionally causing removal stepdown.

connection.explanation: Term/role reset clears election tally, remote replication support and readOnly acknowledgments, while preserving log and committed prefix; current-term matching prevents a fresh leader from advancing commitment solely using an old-term candidate index. Queued/in-flight responses may outlive resets, so Step term checks remain necessary. StorageAppendResp carries both creation term and entry identity: old-term entry stabilization is skipped even if entry term/index recur, but committed snapshot application survives that term change. StorageApplyResp is term-zero and represents committed work independent of leadership. Configuration changes retain existing participant progress but change which IDs count; switching configuration can immediately rerun commitment. Snapshots recover configuration as well as log boundary. Safe reads wait for current-term commitment (except singleton shortcut), track context-specific heartbeat acknowledgments under active voters, then expose read index to a caller that still must wait for application. reset replaces readOnly but does not clear pendingReadIndexMessages; release retries them only after a current-term commit, creating fresh acknowledgment tracking.

Application and public client completion remain separate caller actions; proposal acceptance does not promise commitment.

context.explanation: Ticks or Campaign trigger hup only when promotable and without unapplied committed configuration changes. PreVote can gather prospective support without increasing term; real candidacy resets state, increments term and records self vote. Self and remote vote replies are queued behind persistence. Vote grants require vote/leader eligibility and last-log freshness. Matching response type and active voter quorum determine victory; the new leader resets progress and appends its current-term empty entry. Higher-term messages normally force follower transition, with lease/pre-vote exceptions; obsolete responses are rejected. CheckQuorum can cause same-term stepdown. Transfer pauses proposals, catches the target up and sends TimeoutNow; timeout or ineligibility aborts transfer. Restart restores HardState/log/configuration and starts as follower. connection.explanation: Term/role reset clears election tally, remote replication support and readOnly acknowledgments, while preserving log and committed prefix; current-term matching prevents a fresh leader from advancing commitment solely using an old-term candidate index. Queued/in-flight responses may outlive resets, so Step term checks remain necessary. StorageAppendResp carries both creation term and entry identity: old-term entry stabilization is skipped even if entry term/index recur, but committed snapshot application survives that term change. StorageApplyResp is term-zero and represents committed work independent of leadership. Configuration changes retain existing participant progress but change which IDs count; switching configuration can immediately rerun commitment. Snapshots recover configuration as well as log boundary. Safe reads wait for current-term commitment (except singleton shortcut), track context-specific heartbeat acknowledgments under active voters, then expose read index to a caller that still must wait for application. reset replaces readOnly but does not clear pendingReadIndexMessages; release retries them only after a current-term commit, creating fresh acknowledgment tracking.
